name: Basis criterion
statement: A collection B is a basis for a topology iff it covers X and any point in B1 intersection B2 lies in a basis element contained in that intersection.
conditions: B is a collection of subsets of X.
conclusion: Unions of basis elements define a unique topology on X.
typical_uses: Construct standard, product, and metric topologies.
bridge_lemmas: Every open set is a union of basis elements.
repair_templates: Verify coverage and pointwise refinement separately.

name: Subbasis generation method
statement: A subbasis S generates the topology whose basis consists of finite intersections of members of S, together with arbitrary unions.
conditions: S is a collection of subsets of X.
conclusion: Finite intersections of subbasic sets form a basis for the generated topology.
common_misuses: Treating arbitrary intersections of subbasic sets as required open sets.
bridge_lemmas: Finite intersections of finite intersections remain finite intersections.
repair_templates: Replace an infinite intersection claim by a finite-intersection basis argument.

name: Continuity into a product
statement: A map into a product with the product topology is continuous iff every coordinate composite with a projection is continuous.
conditions: f:A->product X_alpha and the product has the product topology.
typical_uses: Prove continuity of maps into infinite products.
common_misuses: Using the criterion for the box topology.
bridge_lemmas: Projections are continuous and their inverse images generate the product topology.
repair_templates: State product topology and check each projection composite.

name: Metric topology basis
statement: Open balls of a metric form a basis for a topology; a set is open iff each of its points lies in a sufficiently small open ball contained in it.
conditions: d is a metric on X.
conclusion: The metric induces a well-defined topology on X.
typical_uses: Translate epsilon arguments into topological statements.
common_misuses: Using a non-symmetric or non-separating distance.
bridge_lemmas: Triangle inequality gives a smaller ball around each point of a ball.
repair_templates: Verify positivity, symmetry, and triangle inequality before invoking metric topology.

name: Sequence criterion in first-countable spaces
statement: In a first-countable space, x lies in the closure of A iff some sequence in A converges to x.
conditions: X is first countable and A is a subset of X.
conclusion: Closure and continuity can be tested by sequences.
typical_uses: Convert neighborhood proofs into sequential proofs.
common_misuses: Applying the sequence criterion in arbitrary non-first-countable spaces.
bridge_lemmas: A countable nested neighborhood basis at x.
repair_templates: Add first countability or use nets instead.

name: Union of connected sets with common point
statement: A union of connected subspaces sharing a common point is connected.
conditions: Each A_alpha is connected and all A_alpha contain p.
conclusion: The union of all A_alpha is connected.
common_misuses: Assuming a union is connected when the sets do not intersect.
bridge_lemmas: A separation would force every connected summand into one side.
repair_templates: Exhibit a common point or prove a chain of nonempty intersections.

name: Path connected implies connected
conditions: Any two points of X can be joined by a continuous path in X.
conclusion: X has no separation into two nonempty disjoint open sets.
typical_uses: Prove connectedness of balls, spheres, and manifolds.
common_misuses: Using the converse, which can fail.
bridge_lemmas: Intervals in R are connected and continuous images preserve connectedness.
repair_templates: Use a path argument only for the forward implication.

name: Continuous image of compact space
statement: The continuous image of a compact space is compact.
conditions: X is compact and f:X->Y is continuous.
typical_uses: Transfer compactness through quotient and inclusion maps.
bridge_lemmas: Pull back an open cover of f(X) to an open cover of X.
repair_templates: Add continuity before pulling back the cover.

name: Tychonoff theorem
statement: An arbitrary product of compact spaces is compact in the product topology.
conditions: Each X_alpha is compact and the product uses the product topology.
typical_uses: Prove compactness of function spaces and Stone-Cech compactifications.
common_misuses: Using the box topology, where the theorem fails in general.
bridge_lemmas: Alexander subbase lemma or maximal-family argument.
repair_templates: Replace box topology by product topology or restrict to finite products.

name: Baire category theorem
statement: A complete metric space is not a countable union of closed sets with empty interior; equivalently, countable intersections of dense open sets are dense.
conditions: X is a complete metric space.
typical_uses: Establish existence of points satisfying countably many generic conditions.
common_misuses: Dropping completeness or local compactness hypotheses.
bridge_lemmas: Nested closed balls with diameters tending to zero.
repair_templates: Check completeness of the chosen metric, not merely topological completeness.

name: Ascoli theorem criterion
statement: For compact X and Euclidean target, a family of continuous functions has compact closure in the uniform topology iff it is equicontinuous and pointwise bounded.
conditions: X is compact and F is a subset of C(X,R^n).
conclusion: Closure of F is compact exactly under equicontinuity and pointwise boundedness.
bridge_lemmas: Total boundedness plus completeness gives compactness.
repair_templates: Prove equicontinuity uniformly in the family and pointwise bounds.

name: Path homotopy groupoid laws
statement: Path-homotopy classes compose associatively up to the class, have constant-path identities, and reverse paths give inverses.
conditions: Paths are composable and path homotopies fix endpoints.
conclusion: Path classes form a groupoid; loops at a base point form a group.
typical_uses: Construct fundamental groups and induced homomorphisms.
common_misuses: Composing paths whose endpoints do not match.
repair_templates: Check endpoint matching and use path reparametrization.

name: Homotopy invariance of induced maps
statement: Homotopic maps induce the same homomorphism on fundamental groups after accounting for base-point paths; homeomorphisms induce isomorphic fundamental groups.
conditions: Maps and homotopies are continuous; base points are connected by a chosen path when needed.
conclusion: The fundamental group is a topological invariant up to base-point isomorphism.
typical_uses: Distinguish spaces that are not homeomorphic.
common_misuses: Claiming equality for different base points without conjugation.
repair_templates: Insert the base-point path and conjugation map explicitly.

name: Covering homotopy lifting criterion
statement: For a covering map, a path or homotopy in the base has a unique lift once a starting lift is specified.
conditions: p:E->X is a covering map and the initial lift is fixed.
conclusion: Lifts exist and are unique; homotopic lifted paths with fixed endpoints project consistently.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups and prove nonhomotopy of loops.
common_misuses: Assuming lifting without local triviality or initial-point data.
bridge_lemmas: Evenly covered neighborhoods and subdivision of compact intervals.
repair_templates: Specify the initial lift and subdivide the path subordinate to an evenly covered cover.

name: Seifert-van Kampen theorem
statement: If X is the union of open path-connected sets U,V with path-connected intersection, its fundamental group is the pushout of the groups of U and V over the intersection.
conditions: U,V are open, path connected, cover X, and U intersection V is path connected.
conclusion: pi1(X) is generated by the images of pi1(U), pi1(V) with exactly the intersection relations.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups of wedges, surfaces, and cell attachments.
common_misuses: Omitting path connectedness of the intersection.
bridge_lemmas: Subdivision of loops using the Lebesgue number lemma.
repair_templates: Refine the cover or add connecting paths to ensure a path-connected intersection.

name: Classification of compact surfaces from polygon schemes
statement: A compact connected surface obtained by pairing polygon edges is homeomorphic to a sphere, a connected sum of tori, or a connected sum of projective planes.
conditions: A polygonal region has all boundary edges paired by a proper labeling scheme.
conclusion: Elementary cut, paste, relabel, permute, flip, and cancel operations reduce the scheme to a standard surface.
typical_uses: Classify surfaces and compare their invariants.
common_misuses: Applying the theorem to noncompact surfaces or unpaired boundary schemes.
bridge_lemmas: Each elementary scheme operation preserves the quotient homeomorphism type.
repair_templates: First verify proper pairing and connectedness, then normalize the labeling scheme.

name: Fundamental group of a graph
statement: The fundamental group of a connected graph is free; a maximal tree gives one free generator for each edge outside the tree.
conditions: X is a connected linear graph and T is a maximal tree in X.
conclusion: pi1(X) is free with rank equal to the number of non-tree edges (finite rank 1-chi for finite graphs).
typical_uses: Compute groups of graphs and prove subgroups of free groups are free.
common_misuses: Counting edges without fixing a maximal tree or connectedness.
bridge_lemmas: Trees are contractible and simply connected.
repair_templates: Choose a maximal tree and form loops using each remaining edge.
